subject: Sweden's defense push + Indonesia's new central-bank chief
preview_text: Sweden buys French frigates while Indonesia appoints its first woman central-bank governor.

lead.headline: Sweden goes shopping for warships
lead.summary: Sweden signed an agreement for four French frigates, with deliveries expected to begin around 2030 as Stockholm reinforces its navy after joining NATO.
lead.label: DEFENSE

stories.headline: The government raises its growth forecast
stories.summary: Officials lifted their 2026 GDP-growth projection from 2.3% to 2.5%, arguing that domestic demand is strengthening despite global uncertainty.
stories.label: MONEY

quick_hits.headline: Riksbank watches lingering inflation risk
quick_hits.summary: Officials see room to wait while acknowledging that inflation could remain elevated.
quick_hits.label: RATES

quick_hits.headline: Stockholm's fall arts calendar opens
quick_hits.summary: Museums and galleries are rolling out their first major shows of the season.
quick_hits.label: CULTURE

lead.headline: Indonesia gets a new central-bank boss
lead.summary: Parliament approved Destry Damayanti as governor of Bank Indonesia. She is the first woman to lead the central bank and has spoken optimistically about stronger growth.
lead.label: MONEY

stories.headline: Trade returns to surplus, but only just
stories.summary: Indonesia posted a modest July surplus as exports rose, though a sharp increase in imports narrowed the cushion.
stories.label: ECONOMY

quick_hits.headline: Jakarta readies a major trade expo
quick_hits.summary: JITEX is targeting Rp16 trillion in potential transactions and investment.
quick_hits.label: BUSINESS

quick_hits.headline: Jakarta film week announces its opening slate
quick_hits.summary: The program mixes Indonesian premieres with regional independent films.
quick_hits.label: FILM

setup: Sweden is pairing a brighter growth outlook with a long-term defense buildout. Indonesia is chasing faster expansion too, but its new central-bank leadership will have to manage inflation, imports, and currency pressure along the way.
